questions.question: Which Mughal emperor led a campaign against Kashmir, and in which year did it took place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar, 1586**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Akbar**, the third Mughal emperor, launched a campaign against **Kashmir** in the year **1586** to expand the Mughal Empire and secure control over the northern frontiers.
 
• The campaign was a part of Akbar's broader strategy of territorial expansion, which aimed to consolidate the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Before Akbar's campaign, Kashmir was ruled by independent local rulers. By 1586, after significant resistance, Akbar annexed Kashmir into the Mughal Empire.
 
• Akbar's governance style ensured that Kashmir became a prosperous region, and it was integrated into the empire's administration under the Mansabdari system.
 
• This campaign was significant not only for territorial consolidation but also for ensuring the political and economic stability of the northern regions of the empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Babur:**

 
 
• **Babur** was the founder of the Mughal Empire, ruling between **1526-1530**. He was known for his victories, such as the First Battle of Panipat (1526), but there is no historical record of him campaigning against Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Humayun:**
 
 
• **Humayun**, Akbar's father, ruled from **1530-1556** (with interruptions). His reign was marked by struggles against Sher Shah Suri, and he did not launch any campaigns against Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• **Akbar's reign** (1556-1605) was notable for his military conquests, administrative reforms, and promotion of cultural integration.
 
• In **1586**, Akbar annexed Kashmir, recognizing its strategic and economic importance. This region was later known for its contribution to art, culture, and trade in the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir:**
 
 
• **Jahangir**, Akbar's successor, ruled from **1605-1627**. While he is remembered for his love of Kashmir and frequent visits there, he did not lead a campaign to conquer it, as it was already a part of the empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kashmir under Mughals:** After Akbar's annexation, Kashmir became a vital part of the Mughal Empire, known for its natural beauty and contribution to the empire's economy.
 
• **Akbar's Mansabdari System:** This administrative reform allowed efficient governance of vast territories, including newly annexed regions like Kashmir.
 
• **Integration Policies:** Akbar's policies focused on integrating diverse regions under one central authority, ensuring political stability and cultural harmony.

questions.question: Which committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** was formed in **1957** to examine the working of the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953).
 
• The Committee recommended the establishment of a **three-tier Panchayati Raj system** in India to promote decentralization and democratic governance at the grassroots level.
 
• The three-tier structure proposed by the Committee consisted of:
 
 
• **Gram Panchayat** at the village level.
 
• **Panchayat Samiti** at the block level.
 
• **Zila Parishad** at the district level.
 
 
 
• The Committee advocated for the Panchayati Raj institutions to serve as **instruments of rural development** and involve local people in decision-making.
 
• The recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee were implemented in **1959**, with Rajasthan being the first state to launch the Panchayati Raj system, followed by Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Committee emphasized the need for **democratic decentralization** to achieve effective governance and development at the grassroots level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of the Panchayati Raj System:**

 
 
• The system is based on the principle of **decentralization of power**, ensuring that decisions are made at the lowest possible level.
 
• The three-tier structure consists of elected representatives at each level to ensure **participatory governance**.
 
• The primary functions of Panchayati Raj institutions include **planning and implementing development programmes**, resolving local disputes, and promoting social justice.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system is governed by the provisions of the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which gave it constitutional status.
 
• Key provisions of the 73rd Amendment include **mandatory elections**, reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women, and the establishment of a State Election Commission.
 
 
 
• **Other Committees Related to Panchayati Raj:**
 
 
• **Ashok Mehta Committee (1977):** Recommended a two-tier system and suggested measures to strengthen Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• **GVK Rao Committee (1985):** Highlighted the need for decentralized planning and development through Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• **LM Singhvi Committee (1986):** Recommended constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj institutions, which was later implemented through the 73rd Amendment.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, is a landmark reform in Indian governance that institutionalized the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• Panchayati Raj institutions play a crucial role in promoting **rural development**, ensuring **social justice**, and empowering local communities.
 
• The system has been instrumental in implementing various government schemes like **MGNREGA** and **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** at the grassroots level.

questions.question: Smart Cities Mission in June 2025 completed how many years?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Smart Cities Mission** was launched on **25 June 2015** by the Government of India under the leadership of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**.
 
• It is an urban renewal and retrofitting program aimed at developing **100 smart cities** across the country to make them citizen-friendly and sustainable.
 
• By **June 2025**, the mission will have completed a duration of **10 years**.
 
• The mission's objectives include improving quality of life, providing a clean and sustainable environment, and applying smart solutions to urban challenges.
 
• As part of the mission, cities are selected through a **competitive process**, and their plans are implemented in phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of the Smart Cities Mission:**

 
 
• The mission primarily focuses on two aspects: **Area-based development** (ABD) and **Pan-city initiatives**.
 
• ABD involves retrofitting and redevelopment in a specific area of the city, whereas Pan-city initiatives aim to implement smart solutions across the city.
 
• Examples include smart water management systems, intelligent traffic management, and waste management solutions.
 
 
 
• **Funding:**
 
 
• The Central Government provides financial support of **₹48,000 crore** over five years, which amounts to an average of **₹100 crore per city per year**.
 
• The State Governments and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) are also expected to match the funding.
 
 
 
• **Progress of the Mission:**
 
 
• As of **October 2023**, substantial progress has been made, with many cities implementing projects related to urban mobility, energy efficiency, and waste management.
 
• Some prominent examples include the development of smart roads in Pune and the implementation of smart water management in Bhubaneswar.
 
 
 
• **Expected Outcomes:**
 
 
• The mission aims to promote sustainable and inclusive urban development.
 
• It focuses on fostering innovation, creating employment opportunities, and enhancing the quality of urban life.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection Process:**

 
 
• The cities were selected based on a **Smart City Challenge**, where they submitted their proposals for development.
 
• This competitive approach ensured that cities with the most feasible and impactful plans were selected.
 
 
 
• **Significant Achievements:**
 
 
• Bhubaneswar, the first city selected under the mission, has made significant progress in urban mobility and IT-enabled services.
 
• Ahmedabad has implemented intelligent traffic management systems to reduce congestion and pollution.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• India's Smart Cities Mission has been recognized globally for its innovative approach to urban planning and development.
 
• It aligns with the **United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 11, which focuses on sustainable cities and communities.

__
 
• The **Henley Passport Index** ranks passports based on their strength, determined by the number of destinations holders can access without a prior visa.
 
• In **2025**, India's passport was ranked **77th**, reflecting improvements in global mobility for Indian citizens.
 
• This index is updated periodically and is based on data from the **International Air Transport Association (IATA)** and independent research.
 
• India's ranking highlights the country's gradual enhancement in **visa-free and visa-on-arrival access** to other countries.

• The **Henley Passport Index** is a global ranking of countries based on the freedom of travel their citizens enjoy.
 
• It ranks passports by evaluating how many destinations a passport holder can visit without obtaining a visa beforehand.
 
• This index is a reliable measure of a country's **global mobility** and the quality of its diplomatic relationships.
 
• The index is based on data from the **International Air Transport Association (IATA)** and updated by **Henley & Partners**.
 
 
 
• **India's Passport Evolution:**
 
 
• India's passport ranking has shown improvement in recent years due to **international agreements** and enhanced diplomatic efforts.
 
• Citizens of India can now access more countries under **visa-free** or **visa-on-arrival** conditions compared to previous years.
 
• This reflects India's growing influence and stronger **bilateral ties** with other nations.
 
 
 
• **Top-Ranked Countries:**
 
 
• Countries like **Japan**, **Singapore**, and **Germany** consistently rank at the top of the Henley Passport Index due to their extensive visa-free access.
 
• These nations enjoy high mobility due to strong **economic stability**, robust **diplomatic relations**, and global reputation.
 
 
 
• **Factors Impacting Rankings:**
 
 
• Passport rankings are influenced by factors such as **visa policies**, **international relations**, and **geopolitical stability**.
 
• Countries with weak diplomatic ties or internal instability may rank lower on the index.

• **Henley Passport Index Methodology:**

 
 
• The index uses data from **IATA**, covering approximately **199 passports** and **227 travel destinations**.
 
• Scores are based on the number of destinations accessible without a visa or with visa-on-arrival.
 
 
 
• **India's Diplomatic Initiatives:**

questions.question: The Flamingo Festival 2025 was conducted in ______ from January 18 to 20.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tirupati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Flamingo Festival** is an annual event celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, focusing on migratory birds like flamingos that arrive in the region to nest and breed.
 
• The festival is primarily organized in **Tirupati**, Andhra Pradesh, known for its proximity to Pulicat Lake and the Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary, which are important habitats for flamingos.
 
• The **2025 edition** of the Flamingo Festival was conducted from **January 18 to January 20**, attracting bird enthusiasts, environmentalists, and tourists from across the country.
 
• The festival highlights the importance of **conservation**, biodiversity, and sustainable tourism in preserving the ecosystem.
 
• **Tirupati**, apart from being a religious hub, plays an important role in hosting this ecological and cultural event, emphasizing the harmony between nature and human activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pulicat Lake:**

 
 
• Pulicat Lake is the **second-largest brackish water lagoon** in India, located on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
 
• The lake serves as a crucial habitat for **flamingos** and other migratory birds, especially during the winter season.
 
• It provides nesting grounds for birds and supports rich biodiversity, making it a vital ecological zone.
 
 
 
• **Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary:**
 
 
• Located near Tirupati, Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is known for its **large population of pelicans and flamingos**.
 
• The sanctuary spans over **458 hectares** and is a key attraction during the Flamingo Festival.
 
• It serves as a breeding ground for several bird species and promotes **eco-tourism** in the region.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Flamingo Festival:**
 
 
• The festival creates awareness about **bird conservation** and the need to protect migratory bird habitats.
 
• It provides an opportunity to study and appreciate the **unique migratory patterns** of flamingos and other birds.
 
• The event boosts **local tourism**, generating income for communities while promoting environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Tirupati:**
 
 
• Tirupati is globally renowned for the **Tirumala Venkateswara Temple** and attracts millions of devotees annually.
 
• The city also plays a significant role in hosting **cultural and ecological festivals**, such as the Flamingo Festival, showcasing its diverse appeal.
 
• Its proximity to key ecological sites like Pulicat Lake and Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary makes it an ideal location for the festival.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flamingos:**

 
 
• Flamingos are known for their **distinctive pink feathers**, which are a result of carotenoid pigments found in their diet.
 
• They are **migratory birds**, traveling long distances to breed and feed in favorable climates.
 
• India hosts flamingos primarily in regions like Pulicat Lake, Rann of Kutch, and Chilika Lake.
 
 
 
• **Eco-tourism:**
 
 
• Eco-tourism focuses on **responsible travel** to natural areas, conserving the environment and improving the well-being of local people.
 
• The Flamingo Festival is a prime example of eco-tourism, blending **environmental conservation** with cultural celebration.
 
• It encourages sustainable practices and helps preserve the delicate ecosystems of migratory birds.

• Governments and NGOs collaborate to ensure the **preservation of wetlands** and biodiversity.

questions.question: The Government of India has set a target of achieving 140 GW of wind power capacity by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2030**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India** has set an ambitious target of achieving **140 GW (Gigawatts) of wind power capacity** by the year **2030**.
 
• This goal aligns with India’s commitment under the **Paris Agreement** and its aim to transition to a sustainable energy future.
 
• Wind energy is a crucial component of India's renewable energy strategy, and it plays a significant role in reducing the nation's dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• India ranks as one of the **world's largest producers of wind energy**, with states like **Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Rajasthan** leading in wind power generation.
 
• The target of 140 GW is expected to be achieved through increased investments, technological advancements, and favorable policy frameworks like the **National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy** and incentives for renewable energy projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wind Power in India:**

 
 
• India is the fourth largest producer of wind power globally, following **China, the USA, and Germany**.
 
• As of **2023**, India's installed wind energy capacity stands at approximately **44 GW**, contributing significantly to the total renewable energy capacity.
 
• Wind energy projects are predominantly located in states with high wind potential, such as **Tamil Nadu** and **Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Government Schemes and Policies:**
 
 
• The **National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy**, introduced in **2018**, aims to promote large-scale grid-connected wind-solar hybrid systems for efficient utilization of renewable energy resources.
 
• Under the **Renewable Energy Purchase Obligation (RPO)**, power distribution companies are mandated to purchase a certain percentage of their energy from renewable sources, including wind.
 
• The **Accelerated Depreciation Benefit** is provided to encourage investments in wind energy projects.
 
 
 
• **Global Commitments:**
 
 
• India’s wind energy target aligns with its commitment to achieve **500 GW** of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by **2030** under the **Paris Climate Agreement**.
 
• It also contributes to the goal of reducing the carbon intensity of its GDP by **33-35%** from 2005 levels by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• India has adopted cutting-edge technologies like **onshore and offshore wind turbines**, which improve efficiency and energy output.
 
• Significant focus is on offshore wind energy projects, with the government planning a **1 GW offshore wind energy project off the coast of Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite its rapid growth, the wind energy sector in India faces challenges such as **land acquisition issues**, **grid infrastructure limitations**, and **high initial capital costs**.
 
• The government is working on strategies to overcome these hurdles and ensure the smooth implementation of wind energy projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paris Agreement:**

 
 
• India is a signatory to the Paris Agreement, which aims to limit global warming to **below 2°C** above pre-industrial levels.
 
• As part of its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), India pledged to increase its renewable energy capacity to **175 GW** by **2022** and 500 GW by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy Targets:**
 
 
• India’s renewable energy target of **500 GW** by **2030** includes contributions from **solar, wind, hydro, and biomass** projects.
 
• The government has introduced various incentives, such as tax benefits and subsidies, to promote renewable energy adoption.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Wind energy reduces dependence on fossil fuels, thereby cutting **carbon emissions** and promoting sustainable development.
 
• It also generates employment opportunities and contributes to **energy security** in the country.
 
 
 
• **Offshore Wind Energy Potential:**
 
 
• India’s vast coastline provides significant potential for offshore wind energy, which is expected to play a crucial role in achieving the **2030** target.
 
• The government is encouraging private investments and international collaborations in this sector.

questions.question: Geostationary orbit satellites travel at about ______ km per second.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 km per second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geostationary orbit satellites** are designed to remain stationary relative to a specific point on Earth's surface, making them crucial for applications like communication, weather monitoring, and broadcasting.
 
• These satellites are placed at an altitude of approximately **35,786 km** above Earth's equator and revolve around the Earth in sync with its rotation.
 
• The orbital speed required for a geostationary satellite to maintain its position is **around 3 km per second**. This speed ensures that the satellite completes one orbit in 24 hours, matching Earth's rotational period.
 
• Geostationary satellites are positioned in the equatorial plane to achieve this synchronization and avoid drifting from their designated location.
 
• The velocity calculation is based on gravitational forces and orbital mechanics, ensuring the satellite remains in a stable orbit. *Hence, the correct answer is 3 km per second.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geostationary Orbit Characteristics:**

 
 
• Geostationary orbits are circular and lie in the Earth's equatorial plane.
 
• Satellites in these orbits maintain a constant position relative to Earth, appearing stationary from the ground.
 
• This orbit is highly advantageous for applications like **telecommunication, satellite television, and weather forecasting.**
 
 
 
• **Orbital Speed Details:**
 
 
• The orbital speed of a geostationary satellite is determined by balancing gravitational force with the centrifugal force due to the satellite's motion.
 
• It requires a precise speed of approximately **3 km per second** to remain geostationary.
 
• Any deviation in speed or altitude can cause the satellite to drift away from its designated position.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Geostationary Satellites:**
 
 
• Used extensively for **global communication** networks like satellite internet and telephone services.
 
• Important for real-time **weather monitoring** and disaster management.
 
• Utilized in broadcasting services for television and radio.
 
• Supports navigation systems and space-based research.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites:**
 
 
• LEO satellites orbit much closer to Earth, typically at altitudes of **500-2,000 km**.
 
• They move faster relative to Earth's surface, completing several orbits per day.
 
• LEO satellites are ideal for applications requiring low latency, such as **Earth observation** and scientific experiments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding force?

I. If an unbalanced force is applied on the object, there will be a change either in its speed or in the direction of its motion.

II. To accelerate the motion of an object, a balanced force is required.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** If an unbalanced force is applied on an object, there will be a change either in its speed or in the direction of its motion.

 
 
• This statement is **correct** as it aligns with **Newton's First Law of Motion** (Law of Inertia) and Newton's Second Law of Motion.
 
• When a net or unbalanced force acts on an object, it results in a change in the state of motion, causing the object to either accelerate, decelerate, or change its direction of motion.
 
• For instance, when you push a stationary ball, it starts moving, or when you push a moving ball harder, its speed increases or it changes direction.
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** To accelerate the motion of an object, a balanced force is required.
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect** because balanced forces do not change the state of motion of an object.
 
• When forces acting on an object are balanced, their effects cancel each other out, and the object either remains at rest or continues to move with constant velocity.
 
• Acceleration of an object requires an **unbalanced force**, as per Newton's Second Law of Motion, which states that force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma).
 
 
 
• Hence, **Statement I** is correct, and **Statement II** is incorrect. The correct answer is **Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Force:**

 
 
• Force is defined as an interaction that, when unopposed, changes the motion of an object.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• The SI unit of force is the **Newton (N)**.
 
• Examples include gravitational force, frictional force, and applied force.
 
 
 
• **Balanced Forces:**
 
 
• When two or more forces acting on an object are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, they are called balanced forces.
 
• Balanced forces do not change the state of motion of an object.
 
• Example: A book resting on a table experiences balanced forces—gravity pulling it down and the table exerting an upward force.
 
 
 
• **Unbalanced Forces:**
 
 
• When forces acting on an object are not equal and opposite, they are called unbalanced forces.
 
• Unbalanced forces cause a change in the object's speed or direction of motion.
 
• Example: Pushing a trolley with a greater force than friction causes it to move.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**
 
 
• **First Law:** An object remains at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• **Second Law:** The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass (F = ma).
 
• **Third Law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding force and motion is crucial in fields like engineering, mechanics, and space exploration.
 
• Examples include designing vehicles for better acceleration and safety, calculating trajectories in sports, and analyzing structural stability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's Laws in Daily Life:**

 
 
• First Law: Wearing seatbelts in a car prevents passengers from continuing to move forward when the car suddenly stops.
 
• Second Law: Pushing a lighter object requires less force compared to a heavier object for the same acceleration.
 
• Third Law: When you jump off a boat, the boat moves backward due to the reaction force.
 
 
 
• **SI Units and Measurement:**
 
 
• Force is measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• 1 Newton is the force needed to accelerate a 1 kg mass by 1 m/s².
 
• Force can be measured using instruments like spring balances.

__
 
• **Caste data** in India was regularly collected during the decennial censuses conducted by the British from **1881 to 1931**. The collection of such data was discontinued post-1931.
 
• The decision to stop collecting caste-based data after **1931** was influenced by administrative complexities and the financial constraints of the British government during the period of the **Great Depression**.
 
• The caste-based census provided detailed information on the caste composition of Indian society, which the British often used to implement their policy of "divide and rule."
 
• The **1931 census** was the last census under British rule to enumerate caste data comprehensively. From 1941 onwards, caste data was not recorded in detail, and after India's independence in 1947, it was omitted from national censuses except for data on Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
• This data from 1931 is still referenced in various socio-economic studies and policies due to the lack of detailed caste data in subsequent censuses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The first comprehensive **census in India** was conducted in **1872**, but it was not considered complete or uniform. The first synchronized decennial census was conducted in **1881**.
 
• The censuses conducted during the British era aimed to collect data on various socio-economic, demographic, and cultural factors, including caste, religion, and occupation.
 
 
 
• **Role of Caste Data:**
 
 
• Caste data collected during the census was used by the British to understand Indian society and implement policies that would consolidate their administrative control.
 
• It also served as a tool for implementing affirmative action policies for certain disadvantaged castes in post-independence India, such as reservations for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Census Practices:**
 
 
• After India's independence, caste data collection was limited to the enumeration of SCs and STs for the purpose of policy-making and implementation of affirmative action programs.
 
• There has been an ongoing debate about whether caste data should be collected again in modern censuses to better understand and address socio-economic disparities.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of 1931 Data:**
 
 
• Since no comprehensive caste-based census has been conducted after 1931, this data is still used as a reference for socio-economic and political analysis in India.
 
• Many scholars and policymakers argue that caste data is essential for understanding inequalities and ensuring equitable distribution of resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **1941 Census and Limitations:** The census conducted in 1941 was affected by **World War II**, and caste data was not collected in detail.
 
• **Modern Caste Surveys:** In the absence of caste data from national censuses, some states like **Bihar** and **Karnataka** have conducted their own caste surveys to inform policy decisions.

questions.question: Which ancient Sanskrit grammarian lived during the time of the Nandas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Panini** was a renowned ancient Sanskrit grammarian who lived during the time of the **Nandas**, around the 4th century BCE.
 
• Panini is best known for his work **Ashtadhyayi**, which is regarded as one of the most comprehensive and systematic treatises on Sanskrit grammar.
 
• His grammar system laid the foundation for linguistic studies and is considered a milestone in language analysis and formal systems.
 
• The Nanda dynasty ruled Magadha before the Mauryan Empire, which aligns with Panini’s time, making him a contemporary to the Nanda kings.
 
• Panini’s contributions have influenced not only Indian linguistic traditions but also modern computational linguistics and language processing models.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Panini’s Ashtadhyayi:**

 
 
• The **Ashtadhyayi** consists of 8 chapters and is a concise set of rules for Sanskrit grammar.
 
• It uses a unique system of metarules and technical terms to explain grammatical constructs and syntax.
 
• Panini’s methodology is an early example of formal language theory, influencing fields like mathematics, computer science, and artificial intelligence.
 
 
 
• **The Nanda Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Nanda dynasty ruled between **345 BCE and 321 BCE** in the Magadha region of India.
 
• It is known for its administrative efficiency and significant military strength, which paved the way for the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Panini lived during this period, as is evident from references to contemporary political and social conditions in his work.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributions of Panini:**
 
 
• Panini introduced the use of technical terms like **samjna** (definitions) and **sutra** (aphorisms) in his grammar system.
 
• His work became a cornerstone for subsequent grammarians like Patanjali, who wrote a commentary called **Mahabhashya**.
 
• Panini’s grammar influenced European linguistics, particularly during the colonial period when Sanskrit studies gained attention.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Kalidasa:** A classical Sanskrit poet and dramatist who lived much later, around the 4th-5th century CE. He is not associated with the Nanda period.
 
• **Aryabhata:** An ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer, who lived around 476 CE, also much later than the Nanda dynasty.
 
• **Patanjali:** A grammarian who wrote a commentary on Panini’s work, but lived in the Mauryan period, not during the Nandas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Panini’s Influence:**

 
 
• Panini’s work has been foundational for the study of **Sanskrit** and has influenced **linguistics worldwide**.
 
• His systematic approach to language analysis is still studied and admired for its precision and depth.
 
• The **Ashtadhyayi** is an essential text for understanding the development of ancient Indian knowledge systems.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Nanda dynasty provided a stable political environment conducive to scholarly pursuits like those of Panini.
 
• This period also saw the development of other fields like medicine, astronomy, and mathematics in ancient India.

questions.question: Who are traditionally believed to have composed the Vedic hymns in early Indian tradition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rishis and Rishikas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In early Indian tradition, the **Vedic hymns** were composed by **Rishis** (sages) and **Rishikas** (female sages). These hymns form part of the sacred texts of the Vedas, which are the earliest literary and religious texts of ancient India.
 
• The Rishis and Rishikas were believed to have been divinely inspired and had the spiritual insight to hear and compose these sacred hymns, known as "Shruti," meaning "that which is heard."
 
• The hymns mainly comprise prayers, praises, and philosophical discourses dedicated to various deities such as Agni (fire), Indra (rain and thunder), and Varuna (cosmic order).
 
• These compositions were passed down orally through generations before being written down, showcasing the oral tradition of ancient India.
 
• The Vedic hymns encapsulate knowledge related to cosmology, rituals, ethics, and philosophical inquiry, forming the foundation of Hinduism and Indian culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rishis and Rishikas:**

 
 
• The term "Rishi" refers to a sage or seer in ancient Indian tradition who was spiritually enlightened and capable of divine insight.
 
• Female sages, known as "Rishikas," also contributed to the composition of some hymns in the Vedas. For instance, notable Rishikas include **Gargi** and **Maitreyi**, who appear in philosophical discussions in texts like the Upanishads.
 
• Rishis were often regarded as the mediators between humans and the divine realm, interpreting cosmic truths through their hymns.
 
 
 
• **Vedas:**
 
 
• The Vedas consist of four collections: **Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda,** and **Atharvaveda**. Each collection has its unique focus, ranging from hymns to rituals and philosophical discourses.
 
• The Rigveda, the oldest of the Vedas, contains more than 1,000 hymns dedicated to various deities.
 
• The Vedas were composed in **Vedic Sanskrit**, a language distinct from Classical Sanskrit and believed to be one of the oldest languages in the world.
 
 
 
• **Oral Tradition:**
 
 
• The Vedic hymns were transmitted orally for centuries before being written down, demonstrating a remarkable tradition of memorization and preservation.
 
• The oral tradition involved intricate techniques of recitation to ensure accuracy, including methods such as **Padapatha** and **Krama Patha**.
 
 
 
• **Philosophical Contribution:**
 
 
• The hymns composed by Rishis and Rishikas laid the groundwork for later philosophical texts like the Upanishads, which delve deeper into metaphysical concepts such as **Brahman** (ultimate reality) and **Atman** (soul).
 
• These texts also discuss the nature of existence, the universe, and the relationship between the divine and the individual.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Kings:** Kings in early Indian tradition were often patrons of religion and culture but did not compose the Vedic hymns.
 
• **Scholars from Nalanda:** Nalanda University was established much later, during the Gupta period, and its scholars mainly focused on Buddhist teachings and other disciplines.
 
• **Village Elders:** Village elders played important roles in local governance and social rituals but were not the composers of the Vedic hymns.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct?

I. During the Vedic period the society was organised into four varnas.

II. Early Hindu philosophy prescribed the four stages of life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** During the **Vedic period**, society was organized into four **varnas**, namely **Brahmins** (priests and scholars), **Kshatriyas** (warriors and rulers), **Vaishyas** (merchants and agriculturists), and **Shudras** (laborers and service providers). This classification was based on occupation and duties, and it played a significant role in shaping the socio-economic structure of ancient India. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• **Statement II:** Early Hindu philosophy prescribed the **four stages of life**, known as **ashramas**. These stages are **Brahmacharya** (student life), **Grihastha** (householder life), **Vanaprastha** (retired life), and **Sannyasa** (renunciation). Each stage emphasized specific duties and responsibilities, contributing to an individual's spiritual and social development. *Hence, statement II is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Varna System:**

 
 
• It was a social division based on occupation and responsibilities rather than birth during the **early Vedic period**.
 
• The system evolved over time and became rigid during the **later Vedic period**, leading to social stratification.
 
• The **Brahmins** performed religious rituals, the **Kshatriyas** protected the land, the **Vaishyas** engaged in trade and agriculture, and the **Shudras** provided labor and services.
 
 
 
• **Ashramas:**
 
 
• These stages reflect the **philosophy of life** in Hinduism, encouraging individuals to fulfill their duties in each stage.
 
• The **Brahmacharya** stage focused on education and discipline; the **Grihastha** stage emphasized family and societal responsibilities.
 
• During **Vanaprastha**, individuals prepared for spiritual pursuits, and **Sannyasa** involved renouncing worldly attachments to seek liberation (**Moksha**).
 
 
 
• **Vedic Philosophy:**
 
 
• The Vedic texts, including the **Rigveda**, **Samaveda**, **Yajurveda**, and **Atharvaveda**, were foundational to Hindu thought and practices.
 
• The Vedic period saw the development of concepts such as **Dharma** (duty), **Karma** (actions), and **Moksha** (liberation).
 
• The philosophical teachings were later elaborated upon in the **Upanishads** and **Puranas**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Religion:**
 
 
• Religion played a central role in shaping social norms, education, and governance during the Vedic period.
 
• The rituals performed by **Brahmins** were essential for societal harmony and prosperity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Varna system** and **Ashramas** were integral to the societal and spiritual framework of ancient India.
 
• The Vedic philosophy emphasized the balance between material and spiritual goals, fostering holistic development.
 
• These concepts influenced the later development of Indian society and religion, shaping cultural practices and traditions.
 
• They also laid the foundation for the **Hindu way of life**, focusing on duties, ethics, and spiritual aspirations.
